references.text: Jesus asks a similar question about whether it is lawful to do good or evil on the Sabbath, when he heals the man with the withered hand: [ref:Luk 6:9|Luke 6:9].
In Matthew, the Pharisees ask whether it is lawful to heal on the Sabbath, and Jesus answers with a parable about a sheep falling into a pit: [ref:Matt 12:10-12|Matthew 12:10-12].
Jesus asks in the synagogue whether it is lawful to do good or evil on the Sabbath, in connection with the healing of the man with the withered hand: [ref:Mark 3:4|Mark 3:4].

The synagogue leader becomes angry because Jesus heals on the Sabbath, and Jesus rebukes their hypocrisy by pointing out that they themselves untie their ox or donkey on the Sabbath: [ref:Luk 13:14-16|Luke 13:14-16].
Jesus argues that if circumcision is performed on the Sabbath, it should also be lawful to make a whole person well on the Sabbath: [ref:Joh 7:23|John 7:23].

Right after the question in verse 3, Jesus follows up with a parable about a son or an ox falling into a well on the Sabbath, and none of the legal experts and Pharisees can answer him: [ref:Luk 14:5-6|Luke 14:5-6].
The Pharisees are divided over Jesus because he does not keep the Sabbath, while others ask how a sinner can perform such signs—the same Sabbath controversy: [ref:Joh 9:16|John 9:16].
A legal expert (νομικός) tests Jesus with a question; this is the same group to whom Jesus here directs his question about healing on the Sabbath: [ref:Matt 22:35|Matthew 22:35].
